rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thabāt, with a ḍamma on thāʾ, means groups: believers may go forth in groups or all together.
rows.anchor: الثبات بضم الثاء بمعنى الجماعات قوله تعالى في سورة النساء يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithbāt means detention; the opponents wanted to imprison or kill the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الإثبات بمعنى الحبس قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك يعني ليحبسوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thabāt denotes making firm or strengthening; the related command فتثبتوا calls for establishing a matter carefully before harming people.
rows.anchor: الثبات بعينه كالتبيت قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال ويثبت به الأقدام يعني ويشد ونحوه ومثله في سورة الحجرات فتثبتوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this use, yuthkhina means to overcome by killing.
rows.anchor: يثخن يغلب بالقتل قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى حتى يثخن في الأرض يعني يغلب بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athkhantumūhum means that the enemy has been captured, after which prisoners are bound.
rows.anchor: الإثخان الأسر قوله تعالى في سورة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق أي أسرتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqifū means find. The verse says humiliation follows them wherever found, except under a covenant with God or people; the other verse says to fight them wherever found.
rows.anchor: ثقفوا بمعنى وجدوا قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران ضربت عليهم الذلة أينما ثقفوا أي الجزية أينما وجدوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yathqafūkum means overpower or defeat you; if they prevail, they become your enemies in killing.
rows.anchor: يثقفوكم يغلبوكم قوله تعالى في سورة الممتحنة إن يثقفوكم أي يغلبوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء أي في القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqafa here means capture: the reference is to Banū Qurayẓa, whose fate is to deter those behind them.
rows.anchor: الثالث ثقف أسر قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athqāl means provisions and possessions carried on a journey, including supplies and provisions.
rows.anchor: الأثقال بمعنى الزاد والمتاع قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s athqāl are its buried treasures and its dead.
rows.anchor: الأثقال الكنوز والأموات قوله تعالى في سورة الزلزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqīl describes something immense in severity, rank, and majesty, as with the dreadful Day and the weighty Qur’anic message.
rows.anchor: الثقل الشدة العظيمة قوله تعالى في سورة الإنسان ويرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Abraham’s trial, kalimāt means the rites (manāsik) that he fulfilled.
rows.anchor: كلمات أي مناسك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words Adam received are the prayer “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves,” after which God turned to him in mercy.
rows.anchor: الكلمات ( هي ) ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا وهي التي تلقاها آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase kalimat Allāh or a common word means the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: الكلمة لا إله إلا الله قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words are the wonders of His making; the oceans could not exhaust them, as the parallel verse in al-Kahf states.
rows.anchor: كلمات الله عجائب صنعه تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s Word in these verses refers to Jesus, son of Mary.
rows.anchor: كلمة الله تعالى عيسى ابن مريم قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words here mean His religion, which no one can alter.
rows.anchor: كلمات الله هي دينه قوله سبحانه في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalimat Allāh also means the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: الكلمات القرآن قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kunūz means money and wealth, as in the accounts of Pharaoh’s people, hoarders of gold and silver, and Qārūn.
rows.anchor: الكنوز الأموال قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanz can also mean a store of learned wisdom, represented by the treasure under the wall in the story of Moses and al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: الكنز المصحف من العلم قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported explanation says the treasure was a golden tablet containing knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه كان فيه لوح ذهب فيه علم وحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akinna means coverings placed over hearts, preventing people from understanding the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: أكنة يعني أغطية قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain aknān are caves and shelters.
rows.anchor: الأكنة الكهوف والأسراب قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takin means to conceal or keep hidden what is in one’s breast.
rows.anchor: تكن تضمر قوله تعال في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʾim describes what remains standing, whether a structure or a person.
rows.anchor: القائم الثابت من البنيان والأشخاص قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawwāmīn means people who speak and uphold justice.
rows.anchor: القوام القوال من القول قوله سبحانه في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean persistence or remaining continually engaged with a matter.
rows.anchor: القيام المواظبة قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright community described as qāʾima is one that perseveres in worship and recitation at night.
rows.anchor: نظيره في سورة آل عمران " أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل " أي مواظبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām means a dwelling or residence; the blessed station and the secure station are fine homes.
rows.anchor: المقام بمعنى المساكن قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām can mean staying or remaining: Moses’ stay among his people, or the time people are told not to remain during the battle of the Trench.
rows.anchor: المقام المكث والإقامة قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām Rabbih means standing before God; fear of this standing is linked with Paradise and heed of God’s warning.
rows.anchor: المقام يعني الوقوف بين يدي الله تعالى قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām can also mean a specific place or position, including the angels’ station and the place where Solomon’s jinn servant sits.
rows.anchor: المقام المكان قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa can mean a force made up of a number of men, as in the calls for manpower in these verses.
rows.anchor: القوة العدد من الرجال قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa can mean earnestness and perseverance in carrying out what was given.
rows.anchor: القوة الجد والمواظبة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa can mean physical force or might, as in the boast of ʿĀd and the stronger peoples destroyed by God.
rows.anchor: القوة البطش قوله تعالى في سورة حم السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwa also means strength and might: God is the Strong, and Qārūn’s company are people of strength.
rows.anchor: القوة الشدة قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddara means to apportion and set measures, including the creatures’ lifespans and provisions.
rows.anchor: وقدره منازل كقوله سبحانه في سورة الفرقان فقدره تقديرا أي جعل للخلق آجالا وأرزاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqduru can mean to know; God knows the hours of night and day.
rows.anchor: السادس يقدر أي يعلم قوله سبحانه في سورة المزمل والله يقدر الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam ṣidq means prior merit or a credit laid up with God.
rows.anchor: القدم المتقدم السابق قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported gloss takes qadam ṣidq as a true prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل نبي صدق وقيل إيمان وثواب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported gloss takes qadam ṣidq as faith and reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل نبي صدق وقيل إيمان وثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A foot’s qadam can mean the foot itself slipping away from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: القدم الميل في القدم قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqdām can refer literally to feet: the believers’ feet at Badr, and the feet of the guilty seized with their forelocks and cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: القدم هي الرجل بعينها قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the prayer for firm feet, feet stand for hearts, meaning that God should make the believers’ hearts patient in battle.
rows.anchor: القدم القلب قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf can mean making an assertion based on conjecture.
rows.anchor: القذف القول بالظن قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf can mean to cast or throw, as in the command to place Moses in the chest and then the river.
rows.anchor: القذف الطرح قوله تعالى أن اقذفيه في التابوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf can mean to command and make clear the truth.
rows.anchor: القذف الأمر والبيان قوله سبحانه في سورة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf can mean stoning: the devils are pelted from every side and driven away from heaven.
rows.anchor: القذف الرجم قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists fourteen senses: intercourse, response, nearness, duration, the closest, the most correct, gentleness, kinship, Jerusalem’s Rock, before death, honor, neighboring, and a sacrificial offering.
rows.anchor: ق ر ب على أربعة عشر وجها القرب الجماع الإجابة مداناة المدة الأقرب الأصوب اللين القربى القرابة صخرة بيت المقدس قبل الموت الكرامة المجاورة القربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm can mean wronging someone by killing; the victim is wronged by the killer.
rows.anchor: الظلم ظلم الناس بالقتل قوله تعالى في سورة الاسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm can mean diminishing something: the gardens lost none of their produce.
rows.anchor: الظلم النقص قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ẓālimūn can mean people who wrong others; God does not love wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: الظالم من يظلم الناس قوله سبحانه في سورة حم عسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm can mean causing harm or loss; the people did not harm God by rejecting manna and quails, but harmed and deprived themselves.
rows.anchor: الظلم الضرر قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة لبني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm can mean injustice: God did not punish earlier peoples without cause; they wronged themselves through disbelief and lies.
rows.anchor: الظلم الجور قوله سبحانه في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To wrong God’s signs means to deny the Qur’an, Torah, or signs by rejecting that they come from God.
rows.anchor: الظلم جحود القران والتوراة والايات بانه ليس من عند الله قوله تعالى في سورة الاعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ẓālimīn can mean thieves, as in the story of Joseph’s brothers and the ruling on repentance after theft.
rows.anchor: الظلم السارق قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulumāt can mean the perils of land and sea from which God saves people.
rows.anchor: ظلمات اي اهوال البر والبحر قوله سبحانه في سورة الانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses are three conditions in the womb; Jonah’s darknesses are night, water, and the whale; layered sea-darkness is glossed as heart, chest, and body.
rows.anchor: الظلمات اي ثلاث ظلمات يعني ثلاث خصال قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness and light can denote disbelief and faith: God brings believers out of the darkness of shirk into the light of faith.
rows.anchor: الظلمات والنور والايمان والشرك قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulumāt and nūr can also mean night and day, which God created.
rows.anchor: الظلمات والنور الليل والنهار قوله تعالى في سورة الانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann can mean fearing or taking heed that a couple will not maintain God’s limits; in David’s case it means knowing that God was testing him.
rows.anchor: الظن الاتقاء قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tābūt can mean the chest into which Moses was placed as an infant.
rows.anchor: التابوت بمعنى الصندوق الذي وضع فيه موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tābūt can also mean the Ark containing a sign of kingship and a tranquility from God.
rows.anchor: التابوت الذي فيه السكينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittibāʿ can mean companionship: “Will you follow me?” and “if you accompany me,” as in the question about Moses’ followers.
rows.anchor: الإتباع يعنى الصحبة . قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittibāʿ can mean emulation or following someone as an example.
rows.anchor: الإتباع الإقتداء . قوله تعالى في سورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Abraham’s way means adhering steadfastly to it.
rows.anchor: الإتباع الاستقامة . قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittibāʿ can mean choosing: choosing a path other than the believers’ means choosing a religion other than Islam, and some choose ambiguous verses.
rows.anchor: الإتباع الاختيار . قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittibāʿ can mean putting something into practice: the Jews acted on what the devils recited and were told to act on God’s revelation.
rows.anchor: اتبعوا عملوا . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittibāʿ can mean praying toward a qibla: the verses describe Muslims and People of the Book praying toward one another’s direction.
rows.anchor: الإتباع الصلاة إلى قبلة . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-sense list also names obedience (ṭāʿa) as a sense of following, though this excerpt gives no example for it.
rows.anchor: الصحبة . الإقتداء . الاختيار . العمل . الصلاة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, al-insān refers to ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.
rows.anchor: الثاني عشر : الإنسان عقبة بن أبي معيط . قوله تعالى في سورة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human in the command to consider what he was created from is Abū Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: الثالث عشر : الإنسان أبو طالب . قوله تعالى في سورة الطارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the rebuke “Perish man,” al-insān means ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab; the same referent appears in the command to look at food.
rows.anchor: الرابع عشر : الإنسان عتبة بن أبي لهب . قوله تعالى في سورة عبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān in the question about gathering bones refers to ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿa.
rows.anchor: الخامس عشر : الإنسان عدي بن ربيعة . قوله تعالى في سورة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān in the command to honor one’s parents refers to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
rows.anchor: السادس عشر : الإنسان سعد بن أبي وقاص . قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human whose mother bears him in hardship is identified as ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr.
rows.anchor: السابع عشر : الإنسان يعني عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر . قوله تعالى في سورة الاحقاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān in the verses about turning away after receiving mercy refers to ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa.
rows.anchor: الثامن عشر : الإنسان عتبة بن ربيعة . قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān in the reminders about creation refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: التاسع عشر : الإنسان يعني أبي بن خلف الجمحي . قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān in the passage about being tested by one’s Lord refers to Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: العشرون : الإنسان يعني أمية بن خلف . قوله تعالى في سورة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first listed use, in means idh, “when”: believers are told to fear God and leave usury, and to remain steadfast if they are believers.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : إن يعني إذ . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also lists mā as a sense of in, without giving an example in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: إذ . ما . ولقد . لئلا . بأن . إن بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also lists wa-laqad as a possible sense of in, without giving an example here.
rows.anchor: إذ . ما . ولقد . لئلا . بأن . إن بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also lists li-allā (so that not) as a possible sense of in, without giving an example here.
rows.anchor: إذ . ما . ولقد . لئلا . بأن . إن بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also lists bi-anna as a possible sense of in, without giving an example here.
rows.anchor: إذ . ما . ولقد . لئلا . بأن . إن بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth listed use is in in its ordinary sense, distinct from the five other functions listed here.
rows.anchor: إذ . ما . ولقد . لئلا . بأن . إن بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īmān can mean monotheism, as in the verses about rejecting faith, being called to faith, and the coerced believer whose heart is secure.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الإيمان يعني التوحيد . قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

words: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith can refer to professing God while remaining in shirk; the People of the Book also accept some scripture while rejecting other parts and the messengers.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الإيمان في شرك . كقوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unthā can mean a female child or daughter; God’s creating males and females means sons and daughters.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الإناث البنات . قوله تعالى في سورة النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unthā can refer to female livestock in the question about which animals are forbidden.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الإناث من الأنعام . قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unthā can mean idols, which the polytheists invoked besides God and called female.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الإناث الأصنام والأوثان . قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among twenty listed referents for al-insān, the excerpt names Adam, his descendants, Hishām or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, Qaraz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Jahl, al-Naḍr, Barsīṣā, Budayl, al-Akhnaṣ, Usayd, Kilda, and ʿUqba ibn al-Walīd.
rows.anchor: آدم . ولد آدم . هشام بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann can mean certainty or knowledge, as in the speaker’s certainty of meeting his account; elsewhere the same root means doubt.
rows.anchor: في سورة الحاقة اني ظننت اني ملاق حسابيه اي ايقنت الثاني الظن الشك قوله تعالى في سورة الجاثية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓanna can mean to reckon or suppose: the person thinks he will not return, or that God does not know much of what people do.
rows.anchor: الثالث ظن يعني حسب قوله في الانشقاق انه ظن ان لن يحور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann can mean suspicion or accusation, as in suspicion about God and the denial that the Messenger is accused concerning the unseen.
rows.anchor: الظن بمعنى التهمة قوله تعالى في سورة الاحزاب وتظنون بالله الظنونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓahara means to appear or become manifest: visible adornment, corruption, and what is apparent of worldly livelihood and trade.
rows.anchor: ظهر اي بدا قوله تعالى في سورة النور ولا يبدين زينتهن الا ما ظهر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aẓhara means to inform or disclose; the verses describe God informing the Prophet of a secret, not disclosing the unseen, or people discovering others.
rows.anchor: اظهر بمعنى اطلع قوله تعالى في سورة التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaẓharūhu can mean to climb over or rise above the barrier.
rows.anchor: يظهر يعلو ويرتقي قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taẓāharā means to cooperate; ẓahīr means helper, and the allies of the enemy are those who assisted them.
rows.anchor: التظاهر التعاون قوله سبحانه في سورة التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iẓhār can mean supremacy and victory: God makes His religion prevail over every religion and its adherents; the believers in Pharaoh’s court are described as dominant.
rows.anchor: الظهور والاظهار العلو والقدرة قوله سبحانه في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓāhir min al-qawl means false or baseless speech, such as the claim that God has a partner.
rows.anchor: الظاهر الباطل قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓuhriyyan means treated with disregard: they put God’s commands behind them and failed to honor them.
rows.anchor: ترك التعظيم قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to retaliate in kind means that if others mutilate you, you may do to them what they did to you, equally.
rows.anchor: في سورة النحل وان عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به يعني وان مثل بكم فمثلوا بمثل ما مثل بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIqāb means punishment itself, as in the descriptions of God’s punishment and severe punishment.
rows.anchor: العقاب العذاب بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀqiba means the end or final outcome of a matter.
rows.anchor: العاقبة اخر الشىء قوله تعالى في سورة الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqbā means the final abode: Paradise for the God-fearing and Hell for the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: العقبى الماوى قوله سبحانه في سورة الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqīm can mean barren or childless, as with a person who has no offspring.
rows.anchor: العقيم الذي لا ولد له قوله تعالى في سورة حم عسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqīm can mean the sterile wind with which God destroyed ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: العقيم الريح التي اهلك الله تعالى بها عادا قوله سبحانه في سورة الذاريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “barren day” is the Day of Badr.
rows.anchor: العقيم يوم بدر قوله سبحانه في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm can mean seeing or observing: although God already knew who would strive, He sees the striving and patience as it occurs.
rows.anchor: العلم الرؤية قوله تعالى في سورة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm can mean knowledge of something and awareness of it, including what people conceal and reveal.
rows.anchor: العلم بالشىء والظهور عليه قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm can mean permission: what was sent down came by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: العلم بمعنى الاذن قوله سبحانه في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn can mean jinn and humans, as in praise of the Lord of all worlds and the Qur’an’s warning to the worlds.
rows.anchor: العالمين الجن والانس قوله سبحانه في سورة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn can mean the people living in a particular era; Israel’s children were favored over the people of their time.
rows.anchor: العالمين عالمو الزمان قوله تعالى في سورة الجاثية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn can mean all of Adam’s descendants, from Adam until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: العالمين من ولد من ولد ادم الى قيام الساعة قوله تعالى في سورة ال عمران
